text: It starts with a phone, in a dark room, ringing.
In a hundred countries, at the same moment, it is in someone's pocket.
One in three phones sold anywhere on earth carries this name.
Then, quietly, the phone stops being a phone. It becomes a computer.
Nokia saw it coming. It simply answered too late.
The company began in eighteen sixty-five, with a paper mill in a Finnish town.
Paper, then rubber, cables, electronics. One company, four industries.
By two thousand and seven it was the largest phone maker in the world. Then the ground moved.
